column1: # The CRSP US-market index's OWN time under water, on the model's definition: share of sessions
# more than 5/10/20 percent below the running peak, fresh-start seeding, from the 202606-vintage
# F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily total return (Mkt-RF + RF) -- the same series and windows as
# longhorizon-2026-08-30.tsv, measured 2026-08-30, read LAG-FREE on a `record_bands -unlagged` copy
# (the daily returns through 1999-03-10 with the stale-price lag removed, an MA(2) inversion fitted
# per calendar five-year block, `unlag_returns`).
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The depth rungs are graded against a relation fitted on 35 FUNDS over
# 2001-2026, and the 0.23.0 valuation cycle pushed the model's d10/d20 readings up (1.28 / 2.74 at
# the shipped default).  Whether that is a regression depends on the ruler: against the modern-fund
# relation's ~0.21 / 0.055 at ~16% volatility, the INDEX ITSELF reads 0.271 / 0.126 post-1954 and
# 0.388 / 0.255 over the century -- ratios of roughly 1.3 / 2.3 (post-war) and 1.8 / 4.6 (century).
# The model's shipped shares (0.24 / 0.126, median path) sit between the fund cross-section and the
# post-war index, and below both index windows on d20.  Since the calibrated membership rule
# (0.25.0) the graded d5/d10 record is the set's OWN index's ratio to the relation over the
# relation's window (SPY w2001w 0.947 / 1.097, QQQ 1.130 / 1.407: one history, where the
# relation's 1.00 is the median of 35 instruments); this file is the disclosure that the relation's
# window has no depression in it and the index runs deeper.  Nothing is fitted from this file.
